content:
Not all power banks are created equal. Some of the best designs I've ever seen feature built-in displays, the ability to charge two MacBooks simultaneously, RGB lighting effects, and a solid metal chassis with two windows showcasing the internal components — Sharge's new Shargeek 300 power bank is truly excellent, and you should at least check it out during the limited-time promotion. Here are some of my hands-on impressions.

Sharge Shargeek 300 Power Bank Review

The brand-new Sharge Shargeek 300 power bank features a solid metal chassis, packs a 24,000mAh battery capacity, and can deliver up to 300W of power to your devices. The see-through design, RGB lighting effects, and built-in display are all major highlights, and it's now available on Amazon at a launch promotion price of US$199.

Features at a Glance:

  • 300W total output — charge 2 laptops + 1 smartphone simultaneously
  • CNC aluminum alloy chassis with advanced thermal management
  • 24,000mAh battery capacity — fully compliant with airline regulations
  • Equipped with dual USB-C, USB-A, and adjustable DC output (5V–28V)
  • Provides stable power for Starlink, portable refrigerators, soldering irons, camera monitors, LED fill lights, and other DC-powered equipment
  • 140W USB-C input — Shargeek 300 charges from 0% to 100% in just 44 minutes
  • Full-tab battery cells — operating temperature reduced by up to 35%
  • 1.9-inch smart display with Sentinel BMS — real-time charging and discharging power curves, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage history, and estimated remaining time

9to5Toys Verdict

If you ask me, Sharge is an underrated brand. Their charging products are among the best-looking on the market, and the brand-new Shargeek 300 power bank is the perfect example.

This thing is absolutely stunning. Not everyone will love this kind of see-through, cyberpunk-inspired aesthetic — exposed internals, RGB lighting effects, and a built-in display — but I love it, and I'm sure you'll fall for it once you see it in person.

What you're looking at is a unibody CNC metal chassis — most power banks on the market with displays are housed in plastic... I really hate that, but I love what Sharge has done. This thing is built like a tank.

From what I've seen, this unit looks absolutely gorgeous — so good I could happily display it on my desk as a decorative piece.

This brand's products have never disappointed me, never had any issues, and frankly, if you haven't been paying attention yet, you really should be. That's been the case throughout the past month or so that I've been testing this brand-new Shargeek 300W power bank.

When it comes to power output distribution, the total is 300W. When all three USB ports are in use simultaneously, the two main USB-C ports can each output 140W, while the traditional USB-A provides an additional 20W of power. From what I've seen, charging three devices simultaneously is more than enough, since I rarely need more than one or two devices when I'm out and about.

Sharge says that charging your MacBook Pro from "0% to 50%" using USB-C1 or USB-C2 alone takes around 25 to 30 minutes. My test results matched exactly — my 14-inch Pro went from nearly dead to just over 50% in 27 minutes.

Alright, let me talk about the display. I absolutely love the feel of it — a touch of retro, yet super modern, and I can't get enough of it.

Functionally, it basically shows everything anyone could need to know, plus a lot of stuff I don't need to know — real-time charging status, discharge power curves that I don't really care about but love looking at, individual cell voltages, cycle counts, usage history, and so on. As far as I can tell, everything works beautifully, and more importantly, every time I take it out to use it, it gives me a Blade Runner or Cyberpunk 2077 kind of vibe.

For power enthusiasts and true professionals who can make good use of this kind of charging and voltage analytics data, this is the most comprehensive set of power data I've seen on any consumer-grade power bank.

Well, I've found my new favorite power bank — this thing performs as well as it looks, and it will be a part of my everyday kit for the foreseeable future.
